claims.text: The initial material is zirconium-alloy cladding with an elemental Cr coating.
Adding a minor amount of Al to the Cr coating will improve coating durability.
Al addition will form a stable CrAl phase.
Al addition will form an alumina passivating layer.
The CrAl phase will act as a barrier to Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The alumina layer will act as a barrier to oxidation.
The alumina passivating layer will improve oxidation resistance in aqueous reactor conditions.
The alumina passivating layer will improve oxidation resistance in high-temperature steam.
The combined CrAl and alumina barriers will sustain coating integrity under cyclic service and transient accident conditions.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr+Al coating will have improved oxidation resistance in both service regimes.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr+Al coating will exhibit less interfacial element transport.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr+Al coating will maintain better coating integrity across both service regimes.
Unmodified elemental Cr coatings suffer premature failure because of Cr–Zr interdiffusion, particularly in high-temperature steam.
The proposed coating is intended for subcritical reactor-water exposure at approximately 285°C, including exposure for about 1000 hours.
The proposed coating is intended for transient steam exposure at approximately 1200°C.
Al content must be optimized to avoid deleterious phases or compromised mechanical properties.
Analogous refractory high-entropy-alloy composition strategies suggest that Al incorporation can enhance durability.
The optimum Al concentration and long-term dual-environment performance remain unknown.
